title: Fisherman sees an orb explode off Ubatuba and collects fragments

tellings.quote: One of the most interesting samples Nolan mentions is from Uba Tuba, Brazil, where [music] a fisherman witnessed an exploding orb off the coast and collected some of the parts.
So, um, this fisherman sees this thing zigzagging, flying in a sort of a pattern. It blows up on the beach and fragments fall out. He then mails this to Ibrahim Sueed.
tellings.difference: Adds that the object zigzagged, that the fragments were mailed to Ibrahim Sued, and that Vallee was involved.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the 1957 Ubatuba fisherman who saw an object explode off the coast and kept the fragments that later reached Nolan.

as_told.title: Ubatuba magnesium fragments
as_told.place_text: Ubatuba beach, São Paulo, Brazil; Stanford lab

plain: In 1957, a fisherman off Ubatuba on the coast of Brazil is said to have watched a glowing ball zigzag through the sky and then blow apart, and he gathered pieces that fell onto the beach and mailed them to a man named Ibrahim Sued. Michels tells it twice: first as one of the samples the Stanford scientist Garry Nolan studies, and later adding the zigzag flight, the mailing and a link to the researcher Jacques Vallée. If true, those fragments would be physical pieces of an unknown flying object.
